summary: Fiona Ross studied at SOAS University of London and works in Indology and other fields. She held posts at the University of Reading around 2003 and at Tiro Typeworks.

Indologist Fitzedward Hall studied at Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute (~1839–1842) and Harvard (~1842–1846). He held posts at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1850), Sanskrit College (1853), King's College London (1862), and the India Office as librarian (~1862–1869).

A scholar in Tibetology, Buddhist, and religious studies, Flavio Geisshuesler studied at Bern, Lausanne, and Virginia (PhD ~2012–2018 under David Germano). He held posts at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (2019, attested 2026) and University of Sydney (attested 2026).
Flora Blanchon studied under Léon Vandermeersch and Nicole Vandier-Nicolas, and she taught Jacques Giès.

Buddhist studies and Indology scholar Florin Deleanu earned degrees from Bucharest, Waseda, and Hamburg (PhD under Lambert Schmithausen). He served as professor at Kansai Medical University (1994–2001) and the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies from 2001.
Florinda De Simini works in Indology and religious studies. She held posts at the University of Naples Federico II (attested 2016) and the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (~2018).

Fok Tou-hui worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at the New Asia Institute of Advanced Chinese Studies, The Chinese University of Hong Kong, and Otani University, and taught as a lecturer at CUHK (~1972–1999).
Francesca Fremantle is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at SOAS University of London (~1965–1971) and studied under Chögyam Trungpa (~1971–1987).

Francesco Sferra works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology, having studied under Raffaele Torella (~1990–1999). He held professorships at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (~2002) and University of Naples Federico II (attested 2010).
Francis Brinkley worked in Japanology after studying at Royal School Dungannon. He held a post at the University of Tokyo from around 1878 to 1881.

Francis Buchanan-Hamilton studied at the University of Edinburgh (MD ~1780–1783). Active in history, archaeology, and other fields, he served in the Bengal and Indian Medical Services (1794–1815) and directed the Acharya Jagadish Chandra Bose Indian Botanic Garden (1814–1815).

Francis Gladwin was an Iranian, Central Asian, and Indology scholar. He was a founding member of The Asiatic Society (~1784–1812) and served as professor of Persian at Fort William College (~1801–1806).

Francis Harold Cook, a scholar in Buddhist studies, studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1965–1970). He was a professor at the University of California, Riverside (~1970–1987) and chaired the Numata Center for Buddhist Translation and Research in 1999.

Indology and history scholar Francis Robinson studied at Trinity College, Cambridge (PhD 1970). He served as Professor of History of South Asia at the University of London (1990) and was president of the Royal Asiatic Society (1997–2000).

Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar Francis Vincent Tiso studied at Cornell, Harvard, and Columbia/Union Theological Seminary (doctorate ~1980–1989). He teaches Tibetan Buddhism at the Pontifical Gregorian University and has been a visiting lecturer at Sapienza University of Rome.
Indologist Francis Wilford was a fellow member of The Asiatic Society (~1784–1822) and served as secretary to the committee at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1799–1822).

Francis William Bain studied at Westminster School and Christ Church, Oxford (~1882–1889). Active in history, archaeology, and Indology, he served as Professor of History and Political Economy at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (~1892–1919).

Francis Woodman Cleaves, active in Sinology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics, studied at Dartmouth and Harvard (PhD ~1934–1942), and under Paul Pelliot (1935). He served as professor at Harvard University from 1941 to 1980.

Francis X. Clooney studied at Fordham and Chicago (doctorate ~1979–1984). Active in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy, he was a professor at Boston College (1984–2005) before becoming Parkman Professor of Divinity at Harvard in 2005.
Francisco García Ayuso worked in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Munich under Martin Haug between approximately 1869 and 1871.
